subject:
Dedicated capacity sizing 



follow-up & requested inputs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jennifer Smith <j.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up & requested inputs

Hi Jennifer / Tom -

Thanks again for the call today - great to meet the Acme infra and product team. Quick recap and the key inputs we need to size Dedicated capacity for your use case (summarize from today):

Summary:
- Use case: customer support summarization + RAG-enhanced responses for e-commerce agents (real-time chat + async batch jobs).
- Preferred deployment: leaning toward Dedicated (isolated GPU pool) with VPC peering to Acme network.
- Timeline: target pilot in Q1 2027, prod rollout Q2 2027.

Items we need to finalize to recommend a hardware/configuration proposal: (please fill the attached sizing sheet if possible)
1) Preferred GPU family or constraints: any vendor restrictions, on-prem hardware policy, or preference for H100 vs A100 (80GB/40GB).
2) Throughput targets: peak TPS (requests/sec) and steady-state TPS you expect.
3) Concurrency target: expected concurrent active sessions/streams.
4) Token mix: average prompt tokens, average response tokens, percent of long-context (>4k tokens) workloads, % of embeddings or batch workloads.
5) Latency SLOs: P50/P95 targets for generation.
6) Multi-region requirement / DR (do you need standby in EU or APAC?).
7) Data retention / compliance notes (KMS, SOC2 controls, audit logs) - we have SOC2 summary attached.
8) Procurement / billing constraints: PO lead time, legal review timeline, any contract must-haves.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx (fillable), SOC2-Summary.pdf.

If you can send the numbers on 1-4 above I'll put together a recommended configuration (GPU count/type, expected concurrency capacity, and a ballpark monthly cost). I can also propose a pilot config that we can scale after we run load tests.

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up Wed Dec 2 to walk through the sizing sheet - does 10:00-10:30 PT work for you?

Thanks -
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0198

From: Jennifer Smith <j.smith@acme.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up & requested inputs

Hi Rafael / Marissa / Aditya -

Thanks for the clear recap. See answers below (I also filled the attached sizing sheet and uploaded it to the Drive link):

1) GPU preference: We prefer H100-class for production if available (primary reason: we plan to run 70B+ models and expect long-context workloads). We are also open to A100 80GB if H100 is not an option; procurement can support either.

2) Throughput targets:
- Peak TPS (requests/sec): ~40 requests/sec (expected spike during marketing events).
- Steady-state TPS: ~12 requests/sec.

3) Concurrency target:
- Target concurrent sessions: ~60 active sessions concurrently (each can generate responses independently).
- Some bursts up to ~120 concurrent sessions for short windows.

4) Token mix:
- Avg prompt tokens: 350
- Avg response tokens: 300
- Avg total per request: ~650 tokens
- Long-context (>4k tokens): ~15% of requests (RAG + long-doc summarization)
- Embeddings/batch jobs: ~10% of workload (offline, can be scheduled)

5) Latency SLOs: P95 < 600ms for short-context chat responses; for long-context jobs we expect higher latency (acceptable up to ~2s P95).

6) Multi-region / DR: Primary region US-East; we want a DR plan in EU (warm standby) but not active multi-region for pilot.

7) Compliance: SOC2 required. We’ve reviewed the SOC2 summary you sent; legal will follow up with a short vendor questionnaire next week.

8) Procurement: Standard PO process, lead time ~3-4 weeks. We can start pilot on a month-to-month commitment.

Let us know what config you recommend based on this. Happy to take the follow-up call Thursday Dec 3 at 10am PT if that works better.

Best,
Jennifer Smith
Head of ML Infrastructure | Acme Retail
j.smith@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0123

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jennifer Smith <j.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up & requested inputs

Jennifer - thanks for the fast turnaround and the filled sizing sheet, very helpful. Based on the numbers you provided, here are two recommended pilot configurations and the trade-offs:

Option A - Performance-first (recommended for your long-context 70B use case):
- Hardware: 2 x H100 80GB (NVLink if available)
- Expected steady throughput: ~10-20 req/sec per H100 for ~650-token average with P95 around 400-700ms depending on model variant and batching; with two H100s we expect comfortable coverage of your steady-state 12 rps and spikes toward 40 rps with autoscaling/burst capacity (we can provision additional nodes for short spikes).
- Concurrency: supports ~60 concurrent low-latency sessions; absorbs short bursts up to ~120 with degraded tail latency unless we scale to additional nodes.
- Long-context: H100 recommended for >4k token sessions and model weights for 70B+ variants.

Option B - Cost-balanced (if H100 capacity limited):
- Hardware: 4 x A100 80GB (sharded workload across nodes)
- Expected throughput: somewhat higher aggregate throughput but higher inter-node latency for stateful generation; P95 might be ~600-900ms for your 650-token average unless we optimize batching and KV cache co-location.
- Concurrency: scales well horizontally; better for workloads with many short-lived requests or high burstiness.

Notes and assumptions:
- Model: recommendations assume a quantized 70B family or a 40B variant depending on accuracy/latency trade-offs. We’ll validate with a short load test using your sample prompts.
- Caching & batching: our Dedicated runtime enables KV caching for conversational flows which will reduce tokens processed for multi-turn sessions; we’ll tune batching windows to meet your P95 target.
- DR: warm standby in EU can be a smaller pool (1 H100 equivalent) to meet RTO objectives.
- Estimated provisioning timeline: 4-6 weeks after PO and contract sign-off for Dedicated pool provisioning and VPC peering.
- Ballpark pricing: we’ll send a formal pricing sheet in the proposal (attached draft proposal-ACME-8421.pdf).

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’ll draft a proposal with both Option A and B and include estimated monthly costs and an SOW for a 6-week pilot.
2) Marissa (cc'd) can run a quick pilot plan and schedule a 60-min load-test session with your team to validate latency and throughput on a single node before we finalize node counts.
3) Legal/Procurement: we’ll queue SOC2 evidence and the vendor questionnaire to speed review.

Can we lock the follow-up for Thu Dec 3 at 10:00 PT (Jennifer confirmed Thu works)? I’ll calendar an invite with a pre-call checklist.

Thanks -
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0198
